content.user_title: Review Code Changes with Structured Guidance
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss quality, security, and maintainability issues when teams lack a consistent checklist. This skill provides review prompts, reference guidance, and simple scripts for repeatable review reports.
actual_capabilities: Provides a checklist-based workflow for reviewing pull requests and local changes.
Includes Python scripts that validate a target path and emit basic JSON results.
Documents review areas for code quality, performance, security, and maintainability.
Generates simple terminal reports with target, status, and finding counts.
Supports common development stacks through language and framework guidance.
limitations: The included scripts are lightweight templates and do not perform deep static analysis.
Users must interpret findings and verify issues against the actual codebase.
Command examples are generic and may need adjustment for each project.
The skill does not replace specialized security scanners or CI policy checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to organize feedback before approving or requesting changes on a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Criteria
use_cases.description: Apply shared quality, security, and maintainability questions across reviewers and repositories.

use_cases.title: Create a Lightweight Review Report
use_cases.description: Run the included scripts to produce a simple report that can be attached to a review workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change using the code-reviewer checklist. Focus on correctness, readability, tests, and obvious security issues.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Risk Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a medium pull request before merge
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request for regressions, missing tests, unsafe inputs, performance risks, and maintainability concerns. Return prioritized findings with file references.

prompt_templates.title: Security and Quality Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Review code that handles external input or sensitive data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer guidance to inspect this change for input validation, authentication, authorization, secret handling, and error handling risks.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release readiness review using the checklist and reference guidance. Include correctness risks, operational risks, migration concerns, test gaps, and recommended follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that changes an API handler and adds a database query.
output: High priority: verify authorization before returning user records.
Medium priority: add tests for empty result and permission-denied paths.
Low priority: simplify duplicated response formatting.

output_examples.input: Run a lightweight quality check for a local project path.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the reviewed target, confirms the run status, and lists the number of findings for follow-up.

output_examples.input: Prepare feedback for a team review meeting.
output: Security and performance concerns are separated from style feedback.
Action items are written as clear reviewer comments.

best_practices: Use the checklist before merge and verify each issue against the actual diff.
Prioritize correctness, security, and data safety before style feedback.
Run project tests or CI checks after applying review suggestions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generic script output as proof that a codebase is secure.
Do not copy deployment commands into production without environment review.
Do not approve changes based only on automated checks when logic changed.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically review my pull request?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and lightweight scripts, but the user or agent must inspect the actual changes and apply judgment.

faq.question: Can it find security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can guide a security-focused review, but it is not a complete vulnerability scanner.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The documentation mentions TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Swift, Kotlin, and common web frameworks.

faq.question: Does it modify source code?
faq.answer: The included scripts do not modify source files. They can write a JSON report when the user provides an output path.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Should this replace CI checks?
faq.answer: No. Use it with tests, linters, type checks, security scanners, and human review.
